senses.def: the arrangement of things in a straight line or correct position
examples: The car pulls to the right, so the wheel alignment needs checking.
Use the ruler to check the alignment of the shelves.

senses.def: agreement or support between groups, ideas or goals
examples: The new policy is in alignment with company values.
Political alignments shifted after the election.

senses.def: very similar to each other
examples: The twins look so alike that even their teachers mix them up.
No two fingerprints are alike.

senses.def: in a similar way, or used to mean 'both' or 'equally'
examples: The two brothers even dress alike.
The show is popular with adults and children alike.

note: Not used before a noun: "The houses are alike", not "the alike houses". "Great minds think alike" is a common joke.

senses.def: living; not dead
examples: Doctors said he was lucky to be alive after the crash.
Are your grandparents still alive?

senses.def: full of energy and activity, or continuing to exist
examples: The streets come alive at night during the festival.
They're trying to keep the old traditions alive.

note: Not used before a noun: "The fish is alive" but "a live fish" or "a living creature".

senses.def: the whole number or amount of something
examples: All the students passed the exam.
She spent all her money on clothes.

senses.def: everyone or everything; the whole number or amount
examples: All of my friends were at the party.
That's all I know about it.

senses.def: completely
examples: She was dressed all in black.
I'm all alone this weekend.

note: "Not at all" = hiç. "All along" = from the beginning. With pronouns use "all of": all of us (not "all us").

senses.def: acceptable or good enough; also safe or not hurt
examples: The food was all right, but nothing special.
Are you all right? That looked like a bad fall.

senses.def: in an acceptable or satisfactory way
examples: Did the interview go all right?
I think she's doing all right in her new job.

senses.def: used to agree, check that someone understands, or start a new topic
examples: "Can you pick me up at eight?" "All right."
All right, let's get started.

note: "Alright" is a common informal spelling, but "all right" is standard in formal writing.

senses.def: a public claim, made without proof, that someone has done something wrong or illegal
examples: The senator denied the allegations of fraud.
Police are investigating allegations of abuse at the care home.

senses.def: to say that something is true, usually that someone did something wrong, without giving proof
examples: The lawsuit alleges that the company hid safety problems.
She was alleged to have taken bribes.

note: Common in news and legal English. "The alleged thief" = the person said to be the thief (not yet proven).

senses.def: according to what people say, although it has not been proved
examples: The man allegedly stole three cars before he was caught.
The documents were allegedly destroyed after the meeting.

senses.def: an agreement between countries, parties or groups to work together for shared goals
examples: The two parties formed an alliance to win the election.
NATO is a military alliance of North American and European countries.

senses.def: a group of people or organizations working together
examples: The airline is part of a global alliance with other carriers.

senses.def: to officially give money, time or resources to someone or something for a particular purpose
examples: The city allocated $2 million to repair the roads.
Each team is allocated thirty minutes to present.

senses.def: an amount of money, space or time given for a particular purpose
examples: The school's budget allocation for sports was cut in half.
Each department receives an annual allocation of funds.

senses.def: the process of dividing and giving out resources
examples: The allocation of seats was decided by lottery.

senses.def: to let someone do something or let something happen
examples: Dogs are not allowed in the restaurant.
My parents didn't allow me to stay out late.

senses.def: to make it possible for someone to do something
examples: The new app allows users to pay with their phones.
The money will allow us to hire more staff.

senses.def: to plan for a certain amount of time or money to be available
examples: Allow at least two hours for the drive to the airport.

note: Allow someone TO do something, but let someone DO something. "Allow for" = take into account.

senses.def: money that parents regularly give to their children
examples: My kids get a weekly allowance of ten dollars.
She saved her allowance to buy a bike.

senses.def: an amount of money or something else that you are allowed or given for a purpose
examples: Employees get a travel allowance for business trips.
The baggage allowance is one 50-pound bag.

note: "Make allowances for" = be more tolerant because of someone's situation. British English calls a child's allowance "pocket money".

senses.def: a country that has agreed to support another, especially in war
examples: The US and its allies agreed to impose sanctions.
Britain was America's closest ally during the war.

senses.def: a person who helps and supports someone, especially in a disagreement or campaign
examples: She was a close ally of the mayor for many years.

senses.tr: (ally yourself with) ittifak kurmak, -in yanında yer almak
senses.def: to join with or support another person, group or country
examples: The small party allied itself with the opposition.

senses.def: very nearly but not completely
examples: It's almost midnight; we should go home.
I almost missed the bus this morning.

note: Say "almost all students" or "almost every day", not "almost students". With negatives, "almost nothing" = hemen hiçbir şey.

senses.def: without any other people
examples: She lives alone in a small apartment.
I don't like being alone in the house at night.

senses.def: without help from other people
examples: He built the cabin alone.
You shouldn't walk home alone after dark.

senses.def: only; used after a noun to emphasize that one thing is enough
examples: The rent alone costs half my salary.
You alone can make this decision.

note: "Alone" is neutral (no one with you); "lonely" means sad because you're alone. "Let alone" = not to mention, hele hele.

senses.def: from one end toward the other end of something, or beside it
examples: We walked along the beach at sunset.
There are trees along both sides of the road.

senses.def: moving forward
examples: The line moved along slowly.
Move along, please, there's nothing to see.

senses.def: with someone, or to a place where someone is
examples: We're going to the lake; why don't you come along?
She brought her sister along to the party.

note: "Get along (with)" = anlaşmak, geçinmek. "Along with" = together with.

senses.def: next to or at the side of something
examples: A police car pulled up alongside us at the light.
The path runs alongside the river.

senses.def: together with someone or something, or at the same time
examples: She worked alongside some of the top scientists in the field.
The museum displays modern art alongside ancient pieces.

senses.def: before now or before a particular time, often sooner than expected
examples: I've already eaten, thanks.
When we arrived, the movie had already started.

senses.def: used to show surprise that something happened so early
examples: Is it 5 o'clock already?
You're leaving already?

note: In American English, the simple past is also common: "I already ate." Don't confuse with "all ready" (completely ready).

senses.def: in addition; too
examples: She speaks French and also a little Japanese.
The hotel has a pool. It also has a gym.

note: "Also" usually goes before the main verb but after "be": "I also like it", "She is also tired". At the end of a sentence, use "too".

senses.def: to become different, or to make someone or something different
examples: The new evidence completely altered the course of the trial.
The city has altered a lot since I was a kid.

senses.def: to change clothes so they fit better
examples: I need to have these pants altered; they're too long.

note: More formal than "change". Sounds the same as "altar" (sunak).

senses.def: something you can choose instead of something else
examples: Tofu is a popular alternative to meat.
We had no alternative but to cancel the trip.

senses.def: able to be used instead of something else
examples: The road is closed, so take an alternative route.
Solar power is an important alternative energy source.

senses.def: different from what is usual or traditional
examples: She's interested in alternative medicine like acupuncture.

senses.def: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement seem surprising
examples: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
She still got the job, although she had no experience.

senses.def: but; used to add a comment that makes the previous statement weaker
examples: I think he's right, although I'm not completely sure.

note: Don't use "but" in the same sentence: "Although it was late, we stayed" (not "...late, but we stayed").

senses.def: completely; in every way
examples: The noise stopped altogether after midnight.
I'm not altogether sure this is a good idea.

senses.def: including everything; in total
examples: Altogether, the trip cost about $3,000.
There were twenty people altogether.

senses.tr: genel olarak, her şeyi göz önünde tutarsak
senses.def: considering everything
examples: Altogether, it was a pretty good year for the company.

note: Don't confuse with "all together" (everyone in one place/at once): "Let's sing it all together."

senses.def: a light, silver-gray metal used for making cans, foil, cookware and aircraft parts
examples: Wrap the fish in aluminum foil before grilling.
Recycling aluminum cans saves a lot of energy.

note: American spelling and pronunciation: aluminum /əˈluːmɪnəm/. British: aluminium /ˌæljəˈmɪniəm/.

senses.def: at all times or on every occasion
examples: She always takes the bus to work.
I'll always remember that summer.

senses.def: used with continuous tenses to complain that something happens too often
examples: He's always leaving his dirty socks on the floor.

senses.def: used to suggest another possible action
examples: If the hotel is full, you can always stay with us.

note: Goes before the main verb but after "be": "She always calls", "She is always late".

senses.def: doing an activity for pleasure, not as a paid job
examples: He's an amateur photographer who shoots weddings on weekends.
The festival features amateur theater groups.

senses.def: a person who does a sport or activity for pleasure rather than as a job
examples: The tournament is open to both amateurs and professionals.

senses.def: a person who is not skilled at something
examples: The repairs look like they were done by a bunch of amateurs.

note: Opposite: professional. "Amateurish" is always negative (unskilled).

senses.def: very surprised
examples: I was amazed at how quickly she learned to play the guitar.
We were amazed to see snow in April.

note: -ed describes how you feel (I'm amazed); -ing describes what causes the feeling (it's amazing).

senses.def: very surprising, especially in a way that you like or admire
examples: The view from the top of the mountain was amazing.
It's amazing how much kids learn in their first years.

senses.def: a senior official who represents their country in a foreign country
examples: The US ambassador to Turkey met with the foreign minister.
The country recalled its ambassador after the dispute.

senses.def: a person who represents or promotes an organization, activity or brand
examples: The athlete is a brand ambassador for a sportswear company.

senses.def: something that you very much want to do or achieve
examples: Her ambition is to open her own restaurant.
He finally achieved his lifelong ambition of climbing Everest.

senses.def: a strong desire to be successful, powerful or rich
examples: She's smart, but she lacks ambition.
His political ambition worried his rivals.

note: In English, "ambition" is usually neutral or positive; Turkish "hırs" can sound more negative.

senses.def: determined to be successful, rich or powerful
examples: She's a young, ambitious lawyer who works seventy hours a week.
He was ambitious from an early age.

senses.def: (of a plan) needing a lot of effort, money or skill to succeed
examples: The city has an ambitious plan to plant a million trees.
Finishing by June is a very ambitious target.

senses.def: a vehicle with medical equipment used to take sick or injured people to the hospital
examples: Someone call an ambulance! He's not breathing.
The ambulance arrived within ten minutes.

note: In the US you call 911 for an ambulance. The crew are "paramedics" or "EMTs".

senses.def: to change a law, document or statement slightly to correct or improve it
examples: Congress voted to amend the tax law.
The contract was amended to include a new deadline.

note: "Make amends" = to do something to show you're sorry for a wrong you did.

senses.def: a change made to a law, document or proposal, or the process of changing it
examples: The senator proposed an amendment to the bill.
Freedom of speech is protected by the First Amendment.

note: In the US, "Amendment" often refers to a change to the Constitution, e.g. the Second Amendment.

senses.def: during or in the middle of something, especially something exciting or worrying
examples: Stock prices fell amid fears of a recession.
The mayor resigned amid a corruption scandal.

senses.def: surrounded by things
examples: The cabin stands amid tall pine trees.

note: Formal; very common in news headlines.

senses.def: surrounded by or in the middle of a group of people or things
examples: I found the letter among some old papers.
We walked among the crowds at the market.

senses.def: being one of a group, or happening within a group
examples: She is among the best players in the world.
The idea is popular among young voters.

senses.def: used when dividing or sharing something between more than two people
examples: The prize money was divided among the five winners.

note: Use "between" for two separate people or things, "among" for a group of three or more seen together.

senses.def: a quantity of something, especially money or something uncountable
examples: You'll need a large amount of patience for this job.
The total amount of the bill was $85.

senses.def: used in "amount to" meaning to add up to a total or to be the same as something
examples: Her debts amount to over $10,000.
His comments amounted to an admission of guilt.

note: Use "amount" with uncountable nouns (amount of time) and "number" with countable nouns (number of people).

senses.def: funny and enjoyable
examples: He told us an amusing story about his first day at work.
I didn't find the joke particularly amusing.

note: "Amusing" suggests mild humor; "hilarious" is very funny.

senses.def: a comparison between two things that have similar features, often used to explain an idea
examples: The teacher used the analogy of a pump to explain how the heart works.
She drew an analogy between running a business and coaching a team.

senses.def: the detailed study of something to understand it better, or the results of such a study
examples: A careful analysis of the data revealed some surprising trends.
Blood samples were sent to the lab for analysis.

note: Plural: analyses /əˈnæləsiːz/. "In the final analysis" = when everything is considered.

senses.def: a person whose job is to examine information and give an expert opinion on it
examples: Financial analysts expect interest rates to fall next year.
She works as a data analyst for a tech company.

senses.def: a psychoanalyst or therapist
examples: He has been seeing an analyst once a week for years.

senses.def: to examine something in detail, often by separating it into parts, to understand or explain it
examples: Scientists analyzed water samples from the lake.
We need to analyze why sales dropped last quarter.

note: American spelling: analyze (British: analyse).

senses.def: a person in your family who lived a long time ago
examples: My ancestors came to America from Ireland in the 1850s.
She traced her ancestors back to the 1600s.

senses.def: an early form of an animal, plant or machine from which later forms developed
examples: Scientists believe birds share a common ancestor with dinosaurs.

note: Opposite: descendant (torun, nesil).

senses.def: a heavy metal object dropped from a ship on a chain to keep it in one place
examples: The boat dropped anchor in a quiet bay.
They raised the anchor and sailed out to sea.

senses.def: a person or thing that gives support and stability
examples: After her divorce, her sister was her anchor.

senses.def: a person who presents a news program on TV
examples: She has been the evening news anchor for twenty years.

senses.def: to hold a ship in place with an anchor, to fix something firmly, or to present a news program
examples: The tent was anchored to the ground with metal stakes.

note: In American English a TV "anchor" is a news presenter.

senses.def: belonging to a period of history thousands of years ago
examples: We visited the ancient ruins of Ephesus.
She studies ancient Greek and Roman history.

senses.def: very old; often used humorously
examples: My dad still uses an ancient laptop that takes ages to start.

note: "That's ancient history" (informal) = it happened long ago and doesn't matter now.

senses.def: used to connect words, phrases or sentences, meaning 'also' or 'in addition to'
examples: I bought bread, milk and eggs.
She's smart and funny.

senses.def: used to show that one thing happens after or as a result of another
examples: He opened the door and walked in.
Study hard and you'll pass.

note: In speech, "try and" and "go and" are common: "Go and see who's at the door." Strong form /ænd/.

senses.def: a spiritual being believed to serve God, often shown with wings and dressed in white
examples: The painting shows an angel appearing to Mary.
She put a little angel on top of the Christmas tree.

senses.tr: melek gibi kimse, çok iyi kalpli kişi
senses.def: a very kind or good person
examples: You're an angel for helping me move!
The nurses were absolute angels.

note: Don't confuse with "angle" /ˈæŋɡl/ (açı). "Be an angel and..." is a friendly way to ask a favor.

senses.def: the strong feeling you have when something unfair or bad has happened
examples: There is growing public anger over rising food prices.
He couldn't hide his anger when he saw the damage.

senses.def: to make someone angry
examples: The decision angered many local residents.

senses.def: the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees
examples: A square has four angles of 90 degrees.
The ladder was leaning against the wall at a steep angle.

senses.def: a particular way of looking at or thinking about a situation
examples: The reporter approached the story from a different angle.
Let's look at the problem from every angle.

note: Don't confuse with "angel" /ˈeɪndʒl/ (melek).
